set.body:
Scheduling lane: maintenance. Current plan: docs/refactor/PLAN.md. Live dependency edges supersede historical sequencing below.

Current disposition, 2026-09-19; governing docs/refactor/PLAN.md.
Retained with its original acceptance scope; recheck against current code before implementation or closure. Not a prerequisite for the annotation-assisted preview.

Original scope retained below for evidence; fleet procedure/assignments are historical and do not govern single-developer work.

Plan: docs/plans/2026-09-18-best-recall-to-video-mapper.md §3 Phase 2 Scoring channel; R1.

R1 makes the winning label-producing provider a Phase 2 deliverable. No other ticket builds the label interface. Under R2 this ticket closes as not applicable with a note.

Scope:
A typed label interface separate from the score channel, and the R1 provider behind it.

Acceptance criteria:
1. If R2 was recorded at the checkpoint: closed as n/a with a note citing the readout.
2. If R1 fired: a typed label-provider interface exists, separate from the score channel, with a receipt per call and the recorded-response replay mode.
3. If R1 fired: the winning provider is available behind it with its Phase 1a receipt fields, and replaying its recorded responses reproduces its Phase 1a labels exactly (test).

Gate (AGENTS.md SD2/SD6): `sbt -batch clean compileAll testAll` on the merge result, then
`sbt -batch scalafmtCheckAll scalafmtSbtCheck` as a separate run; every test task in build.sbt's
testAll alias reports bound totals (56 at 0e36a7fa, after the corpus modules were added; recount if
modules change); a named mutation witness per new guard, and each compile-time-probe mutation proved
after its own clean recompile; `cd docs-site && npm run verify:examples` when public API or examples
change; fresh-context cold review in a separate pass; the commit body states the evidence and what
it does not establish.

Size: M.
set.title: [maintenance] Phase 2: label-producing provider interface, and the R1 winner behind it (n/a under R2)
